both schemas is classified here, and a gate in each language checks this file against the schema
a REAL store actually creates (internal/store/purge_inventory_test.go via store.New, and
tests/test_db_inventory_offline.py via LocalStore). Add a column without classifying it and both
The exhaustive list lives ONLY here. The prose document explains the reasoning and names the
columns that matter; duplicating the full list there would give it something to drift against.
inherent   — foreign text is here BECAUSE THE FEATURE NEEDS IT. A locator value literally is
the page's text ({"role":"button","name":"Pay now"}); blank it and healing
breaks. Not redactable. Purge (delete the row) or accept and protect.
incidental — foreign text can arrive here but the column does not need it. Redactable in
principle; where we have not, the item says so.
none       — cannot hold foreign text. Verified, not assumed: these are the entries that keep
a cleanup from being sent after text that is not there.

page_path.note: scheme+host+PATH of the page under test; normalize_url (brain/state.py:72-77) drops query and fragment, so ?token= does NOT reach this column. Part of the primary key.

semantic_id.note: sha1(f'{path}|{role}|{name}')[:12] — measured in the live DB as 07ece0d2c1a9

value.note: THE LOCATOR ITSELF. Measured live: {"role":"button","name":"Start now"}, {"text":"Pay now"}. This is the live cache read by every run and it never expires — it holds page text longer than the audit history does.

created_at.note: REAL epoch — the age column purge filters on

original.note: the locator that stopped working. Measured live: {"role":"textbox","name":"Card number"}

healed.note: the locator that replaced it. Measured live: {"role":"button","name":"Complete order"}

ts.note: REAL epoch — the age column purge filters on

identity.note: ADR-082 identity claim; empty when there was none to claim

page_key.note: last path segment of the page URL (brain/replay.py:65-67) — an order id or tenant slug in a real deployment

plan_id.note: measured live: 68e9ff30af99b7e4. An operator-authored plan file could name it freely, but no product path writes prose here.

step_key.note: measured live across 45 rows: hashes only (030865c5f663)

conversation_id.note: caller-supplied free text, but no product path derives it from page or goal

target.note: validTarget (cmd/control-api/main.go:501-503) checks only the http(s):// prefix, so user:pass@host and ?token= pass through intact

error.note: VERIFIED CLEAN, and worth the words: only os/exec spawn errors reach it (cmd/control-api/main.go:623,655). Its cleanliness rests on lineWriter.Write always returning (len(p), nil), which is a property of the implementation rather than a guarded invariant — see SEC-RUNS-ERROR-UNGUARDED.

started_at.note: RFC3339 TEXT — the age column purge filters on

owner.note: ADR-109: the local account id that owns the row. Ours, not the tested application's — a user_id minted by control-api, never derived from a page, a goal or any typed value. Empty for every row written before identity existed and for every deployment with no accounts.

steps_json.note: locators, alternatives, assert `expected` and `intent` all carry page text by necessity. ONE MEMBER IS DIFFERENT: steps[].value / .text hold the TYPED VALUE — a password or card number — in the clear, and that member is INCIDENTAL, not inherent. scripts/collect-live-run.sh:255 already blanks it when a scenario leaves in a support bundle; the database does not. Root cause is not here: the LLM step schema (brain/planner.py:66-79) has `value` and no `secretRef`, while the recorder path carries secretRef fine. Tracked as SEC-SCENARIO-SECRETREF.

config.not_purgeable: live configuration, not accumulated history — emptying it breaks a running deployment. Its foreign text is a reason to stop putting a target and goal in config, not a reason to let a cleanup tool delete the service's settings.

value_json.note: run.target and run.goal can be set through the setup wizard (docs/setup/index.html:1316-1317). Secrets are refused outright by configguard, but a goal phrase is not a secret and is not refused.

owner.note: ADR-109: part of this table's PRIMARY KEY, not merely a column on it — a config document is identified by (key, owner). Empty is the GLOBAL document (the tool, written by an admin or the machine token); any other value is one account's personal document, layered over it. Ours, not the tested application's: a user_id minted by control-api.

user_id.note: ADR-109: minted by control-api; opaque id, never derived from anything the tested application shows

name.note: the login handle an operator chose for themselves — a person naming their own account, not text read off a page

pw_hash.note: internal/identity PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 credential (scheme$iterations$salt$key). NOT foreign text, so a foreign-text purge must leave it alone: sweeping it would delete the account rather than sanitise it. Never a plaintext password and never reversible

is_admin.note: may create and remove other accounts
